citations.assessment: The complete testimony reads Oshaya son of Yehudah the perfumer before Akiva in Tarfon’s name and concerns a flayed animal. The contexts before and after clarify the ruling and dispute.
This testimony about sap under the Sabbatical-year rules reads Yehudah son of Yeshayah the perfumer, before Akiva in Tarfon’s name. It differs in subject from the flayed-animal testimony.

The flayed-animal parallel reads Yehudah son of Yeshayah the perfumer, as in the Shevi’it name, with the same chain. The Bavli instead has Oshaya son of Yehudah. Preserve both names and avoid assuming the two different testimonies concern the same ruling.
